title: Reserved-pool fragmentation caused silent tenant throttling during burst allocations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:

During a regional traffic surge (2026-02-27 -> 2026-03-01) two enterprise customers reported repeated 429/503 throttles despite overall headroom in reserved pools. Initial alerts showed queue growth for several VIP tenants in the eu-west-1 dedicated cluster while aggregate free capacity metrics looked healthy. Root cause analysis revealed severe fragmentation of contiguous slots in reserved pools: the allocator's compaction heuristic failed to coalesce freed heterogeneous-slot fragments (GPU-type/weight differences + preemptible mixing), leaving many small unusable segments. Tenant burst requests that required contiguous slot allocation (for pinned affinity or large-burst placements) started failing silently and hit local throttles even though aggregate free GPU count was adequate.

Why unique / impact: Unlike prior "undersubscription" bugs which were primarily headroom accounting errors, this failure mode was capacity fragmentation — capacity was available but not packable. This produced intermittent customer-visible throttles for mid-to-large burst patterns and affected customers with affinity constraints and larger model sizes. Two customers (AegisBank, EvoraHealth) escalated to SRE/CS within hours. Because the allocator returned "no contiguous slot" quickly, fallback pathways did not trigger autoscaler scaleups, prolonging degradation.

Actions taken and timeline:
- 2026-03-01 02:10 UTC: Customer escalations received; SRE runbook invoked and incident channel opened.
- 2026-03-01 03:30 UTC: Emergency mitigation: deployed a temporary backfill service that rebundled adjacent free slots into coalesced segments and relaxed contiguous-allocation constraint for bursts < 128 GPU-seconds. This reduced immediate throttles for impacted tenants.
- 2026-03-01 07:00 UTC: Hotpatch (runtime-2.4.0-hotfix1) deployed: rapid compaction pass added to allocator on free events and a short-lived heuristic to prefer same-weight coalescing.
- 2026-03-02 -> 2026-03-05: Canary rollout across eu-west-1 and us-east-1 with prioritized monitoring for fragmentation_ratio and contiguous_free_segments histograms.
- 2026-03-08: Permanent fix merged and released as runtime-2.4.1.

Root cause details:
- The allocator maintained per-pool per-GPU-type free lists. A recent optimization (compact-on-demand) deferred compaction to reduce CPU usage during steady state. During mixed workload churn (heterogeneous model starts/ends + preemptible slot reclamations), many small free segments accumulated. The contiguous-slot matcher required contiguous segments >= request_size; with many smaller fragments, it returned a fast "no-fit" result without querying fallback bin-packing logic or considering temporary relaxation for burst windows. The combinaton of (a) deferred compaction, (b) strict contiguous matcher, and (c) autoscaler being gated by aggregate headroom produced the silent throttling.

Fix summary:
- Short term: backfill coalescer service + relaxed contiguous requirement for small bursts + emergency increased headroom for gold-tier tenants.
- Long term: allocator changes merged: continuous background compaction worker, improved bin-packing that can span heterogenous-weight fragments for compatible requests, and an autoscaler hook that triggers a scale-up when contiguous_allocation_failures spike even if aggregate_headroom is non-zero. Added unit & integration tests for fragmentation-heavy churn scenarios.

Telemetry and observability added:
- fragmentation_ratio gauge (free_fragments / total_free_slots)
- contiguous_free_segments histogram per-pool
- contiguous_allocation_failures counter with tenant labels
- alert: contiguous_allocation_failures > 10/min AND fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 -> Pager

Follow-ups / action items:
- (ENG) Create synthetic chaos tests that simulate heterogenous churn and preemptible reclaim patterns. (owner: Marco Chen, estimate 3)
- (SRE) Update runbook to call backfill coalescer as pre-approved mitigation step. (owner: Priya Nair, estimate 1)
- (PM) Communicate postmortem and updated SLA note to AegisBank + EvoraHealth; offer one month of credits. (owner: Daniel Ruiz, estimate 1)
- (DX) Add explanatory doc to Dedicated Capacity guide about contiguous allocation constraints and recommended tenant configuration (avoid unnecessary affinity constraints where possible). (owner: Lila Gomez, estimate 2)
